findings.issue: `const { id } = request;` runs before the try block. A null/undefined or non-object message (e.g. postMessage(null)) throws in the worker's message listener instead of producing an ok:false reply, so the 'never throws' contract (SPEC-08) does not hold for malformed envelopes. The worker survives (an uncaught listener error fires 'error' on the Worker), but AdviceClient#onFailure then fails the shared client permanently, so every later bot decision rejects and useTableSession rethrows it into React.
findings.evidence: No untrusted path: the only sender is AdviceClient#request (same-origin, typed AdviceRequest with numeric id). Reachable only through a future programming error, not by an attacker. worker-host.ts:18 passes event.data straight to handle().
findings.fix: Optional hardening: guard the envelope inside the try, e.g. `const id = typeof request === 'object' && request !== null && typeof request.id === 'number' ? request.id : -1;` and move the switch into the try, so malformed input becomes {id, ok:false} (the client ignores unknown ids).

summary: REQ-025.1 holds: bot/recommend/grade requests carry only {id, kind, view: PlayerView, style|userAction}. botTurn builds the view with playerView(hand, hand.toAct), which copies fields by name: own hole cards, public player fields (no holeCards), board, pots, actions, legalActions. earlierShowdowns is not passed (defaults to []). HandState, the deck and the replay code stay on the main thread; the hand object is kept only as a local staleness token in BotTurn and never posted. Worker loading in production uses new Worker(new URL('./advice.worker.ts', import.meta.url), {type:'module'}). That is a same-origin hashed asset (dist/assets/advice.worker-*.js), with no Blob, createObjectURL, eval or new Function under src/ or in dist. The `?worker&inline` imports appear only in e2e/support harness files, which src/ never imports, and the test-only slow worker marker is absent from dist. The app sets no CSP, so there is nothing to conflict with; a future worker-src 'self' policy would work. Malformed requests with a valid object envelope become ok:false replies. One MINOR: the null-envelope case throws before the try. There is no reachable untrusted input, because both ends are own code. No new dependencies, no randomness added, nothing logged. Failure is fail-closed: worker error or messageerror rejects all pending requests and surfaces the error through React.
